senses.sense_definition: The state of waiting for or anticipating something to happen.

examples.text: The children waited in breathless <w>expectancy</w> for the presents to be opened.
She looked at the door with quiet <w>expectancy</w> as the time for his arrival approached.

senses.sense_definition: The statistical average length of time a person or thing is expected to live or last.

examples.text: Advances in modern medicine have significantly increased the average life <w>expectancy</w> of the population.
The report highlights a decline in life <w>expectancy</w> due to recent public health challenges.

senses.sense_definition: Something that is anticipated or looked forward to.

examples.text: He was the <w>expectancy</w> of his family, destined to carry on the business legacy.
The project failed to meet the high <w>expectancy</w> set by the initial investors.

senses.sense_definition: A legal right to possess or enjoy property at a future time.

examples.text: The heir held an <w>expectancy</w> in the estate that would only vest upon the death of the current owner.
Legal disputes often arise regarding the nature of an <w>expectancy</w> in inheritance law.
